evidence: Caes. BG 1.34.1: aliquem locum medium utrīsque conloquiō
Cic. Phil. 12.26: in Antōniī congressum colloquiumque veniendum est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A conversation, and in Caesar the meeting of two leaders to treat with each other (Lewis & Short). To go into talks, in colloquium venīre; to ask for them, colloquium petere; to negotiate is agere cum aliquō (see negotiate).

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Com. 34: pactiōnem facere dē aliquā rē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The making of an agreement and the agreement made (see agreement); also, in a bad sense, an underhand bargain (Cic. Verr. 2.1.17).

phrases.latin: quī ab eō postulārent utī aliquem locum medium utrīsque conloquiō dēligeret: velle sēsē dē rē pūblicā et summīs utrīusque rēbus cum eō agere
phrases.english: to ask him to choose some place halfway between them for talks: he wanted to negotiate with him about public affairs and matters of the highest importance to them both

phrases.latin: Diēs conloquiō dictus est ex eō diē quīntus.
phrases.english: The talks were fixed for the fifth day from then.

sources: Lewis & Short: colloquium · Lewis & Short: pactio
